finding.title: install.sh ALREADY_INSTALLED probe omits CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER and calls bare JSON.parse, overwriting JSONC settings.json on re-run without --force
finding.detail: src/hooks/install.sh loads installer/lib/settings.js via CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER in the JSONC preflight check (lines 54-75) and the settings merge step (lines 173-181), allowing // comments, /* */ comments, and trailing commas in settings.json. However, the ALREADY_INSTALLED fast-path check at lines 93-114 omits CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER and calls bare JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.CAVEMAN_SETTINGS, 'utf8')). If a user with caveman hooks already wired adds a JSONC comment or trailing comma to settings.json and re-runs install.sh without --force, JSON.parse throws inside the silenced >/dev/null 2>&1 block, ALREADY_INSTALLED falls back to 0, and the merge step rewrites settings.json via JSON.stringify, destroying all comments without updating .bak if settings.json.bak already exists.
finding.recommendation: Pass CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER to the ALREADY_INSTALLED node probe in src/hooks/install.sh:95-106 and parse via helper.parseSettingsText(raw).data before falling back to JSON.parse.

finding.title: install.ps1 ALREADY_INSTALLED probe uses PowerShell ConvertFrom-Json instead of CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER, failing on JSONC comments in Windows PowerShell 5.1
finding.detail: src/hooks/install.ps1 uses node with CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER for both the preflight check (lines 36-59) and the settings merge step (lines 150-222), but lines 80-112 use Get-Content $SettingsFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json for the ALREADY_INSTALLED check. In Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe), ConvertFrom-Json rejects // comments and trailing commas, throwing inside the try/catch block so $alreadyInstalled stays $false and the merge step overwrites settings.json as plain JSON.
finding.recommendation: Replace the ConvertFrom-Json ALREADY_INSTALLED check in src/hooks/install.ps1:80-112 with a node probe that uses CAVEMAN_SETTINGS_HELPER.

finding.title: OpenCode plugin ignores _ctx directory and injects caveman system prompt even when repo .caveman.json sets defaultMode to off
finding.detail: In src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js:280-355, CavemanPlugin = async (_ctx) => discards the OpenCode plugin context (_ctx) instead of extracting projectDir (ctx?.location?.directory || ctx?.directory || ctx?.worktree), calls getDefaultMode() with no startDir at lines 291 and 332, and in experimental.chat.system.transform (lines 345-355) unconditionally appends buildActivationPrompt(mode) without checking whether getDefaultMode(projectDir) === 'off'. Unlike caveman-activate.js:305 and caveman-mode-tracker.js:372 (#634), OpenCode sessions ignore repo-level .caveman.json opt-out.
finding.recommendation: Extract projectDir from ctx in src/plugins/opencode/plugin.js:280, pass projectDir to getDefaultMode(projectDir), and skip prompt injection (while stripping any staleBlock) in experimental.chat.system.transform when getDefaultMode(projectDir) === 'off'.
